full_judgment:
2. In all these 3(three) writ petitions filed under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh respective Rules Nisi were issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inaction and failure of the respondents concerned in considering the lands in question as "commercial" land instead of "Vitta/Bari" and in commencing the tenure for the compensation of immovable property under section 9(l)(ka) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act, 2017 from 13-9-2020 to 13-9-2021 in writ petition No.7409 of 2023, from 31-10-2020 to 1-11-2021 in writ petition No.11432 of 2022 and from 11-4-2020 to 10-4-2021 for the properties in question proposed to be acquired in LA Case Nos. 06, 08, 09 and 12 all of 2020-2021 respectively and fixing award of compensation vide Memo Jari No. 62(353) dated 2-10-2022 relating to RS Dag No.267 under Chariashikar Mouza, Memo Jail No. 65(250) dated 4-10-2022 relating to RS Dag No.101 of Dhopakandi Mouza, Memo Jari No.67(433) relating to RS Dag No.1332 under Chariashikar Mouza and Memo Jari No.60(298) dated 2-10-2022 in connection with RS Dag Nos. 249, 250, 251 and 300 of Dhopakandi Mouza under Ullapara Upazilla, District-Sirajgonj as per compensation rate of 2014, should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect. 

 11. However, the properties in question were included in the schedule of the said notice. Subsequently, a notice under section 4(1) of the said Act of 2017 was issued on 14-9-2021 (Annexure-F1 of writ petition No.7409 of 2023), on 1-11-2021 (Annexure-D) of writ petition No.11432 of 2022) and on 12-4-2021 (Annexure-F of writ petition No.11671 of 2022) on behalf of the respondent No.7 with option to raise objection against the proposed acquisition with direction to remain present on 30-9-2021, 10-11-2021 and 22-4-2021 respectively in person or through his/their representatives for joint investigation of the properties in view of section 4(3)(Kha). The petitioner of writ petition No.11671 of 2022, however, made applications on 12-12-2021 (Annexure-F1) and on 14-2-2022 (Annexure-G) respectively with prayer to classify his properties in question as commercial, but with no response. 

 12. Later, on 22-5-2022 notice under section 7(1) of Act, 2017 was issued on behalf of the respondent No.7 upon the petitioners of all the three writ petitions with a view to take possession of the properties in question. Accordingly, the petitioners were requested to appear on 6-6-2022 in person or through his/their representative(s) before the concerned authority with a view to give his/their statements in support of the claim with supporting documents stating, inter alia:— 

 21. In support of the said contentions, Mr. Murad Reza, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. Mohammad Shahidul Islam and Mr. Md. Golam Hasnaen, the learned Advocates for the petitioners of writ petition Nos.7409 of 2023 and 11432 of 2022 submits that the nature of land shall be determined as per the latest record of right and until the next survey is done, the nature cannot be changed, for, to that effect Gazette notification is required to be published. In this regard, he submits that vide section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, (in short, the Act of 1950) mutation khatian is the latest record of right and for the preparation of mutation khatian, no gazette notification is required. Apart from that, he submits, section 4 of the Act, 2017 stipulates the provision for changing the nature of land which was recorded in the relevant khatian under another nature. Moreover, even after joint survey is carried out the Deputy Commissioner can still change the nature of land under section 4(4) of the Act of 2017. In the instant case, he submits that the respondents did not follow the said procedures. In addition to that the petitioners in their respective writ petitions have categorically asserted that the lands in question are commercial in nature with supportive documents includirfg mutation khatian (Annexure:B-E2 respectively). Said assertions have not been specifically denied by the respondents concerned. In the given context, finalising the award of compensation treating the properties in question as "Vitta /Bari" is unlawful and hence, not tenable in the eye of law. 

 22. He further submits that for determining the assessment of compensation compliance of section 9 of the Act, 2017 read with Rule 8 of the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 (in short, the Rules, 1982) is mandatory. However, the acquiring body in violation of the provision as laid down in section 9(1) of the Act, 2017 considered the 12 (twelve) months period from the date of the 2nd notice issued under section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 instead from the date of 1st public notice issued under section 4(12). As because after issuing public notice under section 4 of the Act, 2017, no land was transferred upon executing deed of transfer with the Sub-Registry Office. For the said reason no deed was found in connection with the respective area mentioning the land as commercial for the relevant period. 

 24. He also submits that the respondent No.7 did not display the joint survey report in the local land office or project area or any public place under section 4(6) of the Act, 2017. To that effect the Chairman i.e. the petitioner of writ petition No. 7409 of 2023 along with the Ward Members of the concerned Union Parishad had issued a statement dated 29-11-2023 (Annexure- Ab of the supplementary-affidavit to the affidavit in opposition). Consequently, the petitioner did not get any opportunity whatsoever to raise objection regarding the said report as the same was done behind their back. 

 31. He further submits that section 9 of the Act of 2017 corresponds to the repealed section 8 of the Ordinance No.2 of 1982. Since no rules have yet been framed under the new Act of 2017 hence, by virtue of saving clause i.e. section 50 of the Act No.21 of 2017 the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 are in force. Accordingly, he submits that while making assessment of compensation of the properties in question compliance of section 9 and Rule 8 is mandatory. 

 36. Article 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, as embodied in Chapter III of the Constitution guarantees right to property but subject to restrictions imposed by law. However, said right is extinguished by way of compulsory acquisition, nationalization or requisition under the authority of law. Vide Article 42(2) when a law/statute, promulgated by the Legislature in exercise of power as provided under Article 42(1), provides for compensation, it should either fix the amount of compensation or prescribe the principles on which, and the manner in which the compensation is to be assessed and paid. Said law cannot be called in question in any court of law on the ground that its respective provision for compensation is inadequate. 

 [(2) A law made under clause (1) of this article shall provide for the acquisition, nationalization or requisition with compensation and shall fix the amount of compensation or specify the principles on which, and the manner in which, the compensation is to be assessed and paid ; but no such law shall be called in question in any court on the ground that any provision of the law in respect of such compensation is not adequate.] 

 38. The Parliament in view of Article 42(1) promulgated "স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহন ও হুকুম দখল আইন, ২০১৭" (Act No. 21 of 2017) (in short, the Act, 2017) relating to acquisition and requisition of immovable property and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto. 

 39. Under the Act of 2017 the process of acquisition commences with the publication of notice under section 4(1) by the Deputy Commissioner " জেলা প্রশাসক" as defined in section 2(5) in the prescribed form and manners, in connection with the properties proposed to be acquired. 

 46. As per section 4(7) after initiation of proceeding for acquisition under section 4(3)(ka) if it is found that any construction of building is or is being made with a view to change the nature/ classification of the property, said change of classification shall not be enlisted in the said যৌথ তালিকা. For non-inclusion of such change in the inventory list is subject to appeal under section 4(8) before the Commissioner and his decision is final under section 4(10). 

 49. Section 5(1), however, provides forum of objection against acquisition to be raised by the person interested before the Deputy Commissioner after service of notice under section 4, within a prescribed period. 

 52. After final decision of acquisition of the respective properties vide section 7(1) and (3) the Deputy Commissioner shall issue a general notice in prescribed form for the possession of the properties in question. 

 54. Section 7(2) and (4), however, have provided an opportunity to the person interested to appear in person on the date, time and place and to place his respective statements of demand of compensation. 

 57. Section 9 prescribes the respective contexts which shall be taken into consideration while fixing the amount of compensation for acquisition of the properties in question. In particular, section 9(I)(ka) provides for taking into consideration of the market value (বাজারমূল্য) of the respective property in question on the date of publication of notice under section 4. However, while determining the market value, the Deputy Commissioner shall take into account the average value to be calculated in the prescribed manner of the properties of similar description and with similar advantages in the vicinity during the 12 months preceding the date of publication of the notice under section 4. 

 59. From a combined readine of the above quoted provisions of law it is apparent that the Legislature has intended to create respective platforms for the affected person to make his stand at the initial stage of the proceeding of acquisition by remaining present in person with supporting documents while a joint inventory list is being prepared [section 4(3)(kha)], which is the foundation for preparation of award. Even, prior to finalization of the acquisition process and taking over possession under section 7, the Legislature has provided scope to the affected person to raise objection on acquisition process and that said objection shall be mitigated after further enquiry. Even, during pendency of the process of taking over possession the person interested is provided with opportunity to appear in person again in order to make demand of compensation in support of documents [section 7(2) and (4)1 and upon making due enquiry thereof [section 8(1)] the Deputy Commissioner is to prepare the award of compensation. In other words, the Legislature vide the above quoted method of assessment has ensured to provide proper and adequate compensation to the affected person for acquisition of the respective properties for greater public interest. 

 60. In writ petition No.7409 of 2023, the properties in question bearing RS Plot No. 267 under Chariashiker Mouja and RS Plot No. 101 under Dhopakandi Mouja, in writ petition No. 11671 of 2022, the properties in question bearing RS Plot Nos. 249, 251, 250, 300 under Dhopakandi Mouja and in writ petition No. 11432 of 2022 the property in question bearing RS Plot No. 1332 under Chariashikar Mouza, Upazilla-Ullahpara were selected for implementation of the project namely "সাসেক সংযোগ প্রকল্প-II এলেঙ্গা হাটিকুমরুল রুপপুর মহাসড়ক ৮-লেনে উন্নতীকরণ প্রকল্প" under "জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রকল্প"। Accordingly, vide order dated 27-12-2020 the Deputy Commissioner concerned issued a public notice under section 4(12) imposing restriction on sell/purchase or illegal construction on the properties in question (Annexure-F of writ petition No. 7409 of 2023). Subsequently, a notice under section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 was issued by the Deputy Commissioner concerned upon the respective petitioners on 14-9-2021 (Annexure-F1 of writ petition No.7409 of 2023) in connection with LA Case Nos 8 and 9 both of 2020-21 and also, in connection with LA Case Nos. 6 of 2020-21 with direction, inter alia,- "উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে স্বার্থবান যে কোন ব্যক্তি এই নোটিশ জারির পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিনের মধ্যে প্রস্তাবিত সম্পত্তির অধিগ্রহণের বিরুদ্ধে নিম্ন স্বাক্ষরকারীর নিকট আপত্তি (যদি থাকে) দায়ের করিতে পারিবেন। ৩০-৯-২১ তারিখ বা তারিখ হতে তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তির যৌথ তদন্ত হবে। যৌথ তদন্তকালে উক্ত সম্পত্তির মালিক বা স্বার্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিকে উপস্থিত থাকিবার জন্য অনুরোধ করা হইলো।"on the proposed acquisition of the properties in question. 

 62. On the face of the said assertions, it is an admitted position of facts that in all the respective writ petitions public notice under section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 was duly published with reference to the properties in question proposed to be acquired in connection with the respective LA cases. In the said notices respective dates were also mentioned fixed for joint inspection in compliance of section 4(3)(kha). It is also admitted that the petitioner of writ petition No. 7409 of 2023 did not appear before the authority concern on the date so fixed for joint inventory, nor has he produced any document whatsoever to show that he made a prayer before the authority to that effect immediate after the date so was fixed for joint inventory nor has he asked for supply of the copy of the joint inventory. Rather, vide order No. 9 dated 3-4-2022 in connection with LA Case No.9 of 2020-21 it has been stated, inter cilia:— 

 69. The petitioner of writ petition No.11432 of 2022, however, admitted that notice under section 4(1) was served in connection with LA Case No.12 of 2020-2021 fixing 01-11-2021 for joint inventory with request to appear on the said date. Also, vide notice dated 22-5-2022 issued under section 7(1) the petitioner was directed to appear in person on 6-6-2022 for making demand of compensation. Subsequently, on 15-9-2022 (Annexure-F) he made a representation with a prayer for fixing compensation along with "itemwari analysis". Moreso, in the said writ petition though the petitioner stated that in response to notice dated 22-5-2022 (Annexure-E) he claimed to have appeared before the authority concerned, but fact remains that his representation is dated 16-5-2022 i.e. prior to issuance of notice dated 22-5-2022 issued under section 7(1), which goes to show that he did not appear before the authority concern on the respective date in support of his respective stand. 

 74. He also submits that the petitioners have based their contention of classification of the properties to be treated as commercial on Circular No. 31.00.0000.036.68.076.17.81 dated 27-2-2019 (Annexure-M of writ petition No.7409 of 2023). Drawing attention to the said circular he goes to argue that vide the same the authority concerned has prescribed certain guidelines to be followed during the ongoing preparation of record of rights subject to certain conditions which is not attracted in respect of determining the nature of the proposed acquired land, as claimed by the petitioners. He further submits that vide clause 3 of the said circular the classification of land has been made in 16(sixteen) classes and clause 4 of the guidelines has specifically mentioned when and how said classification of land will be effected. Further, in clause 4(Uma) of the said circular it has been clearly stated that this classification will not be applicable for the lands which have already been recorded and published in the gazette. Accordingly, he submits that the argument so has been advanced to that effect on behalf of the petitioners, is not tenable in the eye of law. 

 80. On a plain reading of the above it is apparent that said guidelines with regard to classification of lands is applicable for those mouzas where its respective field work for preparation of record of right has not yet started and that the classification of property as mentioned in the last survey published in gazette, shall be treated as correct. In the instant cases, after publication of RS record of the properties in question no new survey has been held in the respective mouzas of the petitioners, as contended by the respondent concerned and not controverted by the petitioners with supporting documents. Moreover, in the respective RS records, the properties in question have not been classified as commercial. In view of the stated position facts and also vide clause (uma) of the circular dated 27-2-2019 the contention of the petitioner as to applicability of the said circular while making classification of the properties in question, falls through.
